text: **Copilot prediction, sealed.** You will shortly ask the agent to *tell me whether my component is being attacked, from the evidence it has.* Write down what it will produce and **name the one thing it will get wrong.** Sealed with items 1 to 4 and opened at phase 8. Name **one thing you expect to be unable to do**, and **one thing you expect to find you did not need it for.** Both specific. Item 1 is the day's honest item and is checked against the receiving party's own answer ninety minutes later. Item 4 is the only self-prediction in the programme that asks a student to rank their own weaknesses across three distinct capabilities. **Item 6 is the ninetieth and last sealed Copilot prediction, and it is the only one in the programme that is about the student rather than about the agent.** **Warrant.** Pretesting three positions before any of them is performed, sealed, and opened after all three are complete — the same construction [S070](/wiki/seminars/S070.md) used at one activity, extended. Item 2 is deliberately loaded: it asks for an attribution as well as a prediction, and a student who attributes a comprehension failure to the decision-maker has answered [S050](/wiki/seminars/S050.md)'s question about who owns a limitation the audience cannot act on. The compression to 20 minutes is possible because there is no framework to pretest — every item asks about the student's own artefacts. **Item 6 is administered before phase 1b and never after, per instrumentation rule 8**, and its two halves are asymmetric on purpose: predicting an inability is the programme's ordinary frontier item, and predicting an unnecessary reliance is the one the dependency-risk provision actually needs. ---
